note: Skills that use the uidaho server's tools: the policy and rate lookups, the check of a passage against university policy, the rates skill that fetches and reports the university's F&A and fringe rates with their sources, and the OpenERA feature-definition interview with its guide (the interview writes to ClickUp through the clickup server's tools, so a client needs both). Same shape as AI4RA/prompt-library's component_catalog.json, hand-maintained. Writing the rates onto a sheet is a client's job (Idaho's mindrouter-365-aware server holds that skill).

components.name: uidaho-lookup
components.summary: Answer a question about the University of Idaho's sponsored-research facts (F&A and fringe rates, budget rules, policies, contacts) with the uidaho tools, quoting each figure or passage with its policy number, effective period or revision date, and the address it was read from; a page that cannot be read yields no figure.

arguments.name: question
arguments.description: The question or topic, such as the F&A rate, fringe for a postdoc, or what APM 45.07 says.

arguments.name: location
arguments.description: On-campus or off-campus, when a rate depends on it.

components.name: uidaho-rates
components.summary: Fetch the University of Idaho's current F&A and fringe rates from the rate agreement and the fringe-rate page and report them in the Rates contract's order (seven labelled items and a Source line), each with its effective period, its document and the address it was read from; a document that cannot be read yields no figure. Laying them onto a sheet is a client's job.

arguments.name: location
arguments.description: On-campus or off-campus. Leave empty for on-campus.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: The project's type, such as organized research or instruction. Leave empty for organized research.

components.name: policy-check
components.summary: Check a passage of a document against University of Idaho policy (the APM and the FSH) and the university's F&A and fringe rates, as fetched from the university's own pages and rate documents, and report a finding for each sentence that disagrees with it: the pinpoint, the sentence's words, one clause quoted with its link, and a suggested fix. Nothing is said from memory; a sentence whose policy could not be fetched is reported as not checked. Report-only: placing a finding on the document is a client's job.

arguments.name: passage
arguments.description: The text to check: a passage of a document, pasted here. Leave empty if it is supplied beside the prompt.

components.name: feature-prd-interview
components.summary: Interview a subject matter expert about one OpenERA feature and write the finished definition into the feature's ClickUp task: thirteen headings, acceptance criteria in Gherkin read back in plain English, the AI first pass taken apart section by section, a blind second reviewer compared and reconciled when there are two assignees, and the criteria fingerprinted against the index task. Never takes attachments or the contents of a real record. Its facts come from openera-feature-guide; its ClickUp work is the clickup server's tools, so a client needs both servers.

arguments.name: feature
arguments.description: The feature's roadmap ID or task name (such as A9). Leave empty to work the person's queue of feature tasks.

components.name: openera-feature-guide
components.summary: The facts of the University of Idaho's OpenERA feature-definition work: the OpenERA list and the feature tag, the Roadmap status block and the AI first pass with its Basis tags, the pass and discrepancy subtask names and the markers inside a definition, the thirteen headings, the shape of an acceptance criterion, the data a definition never holds, the connected systems, the acceptance-criteria index task with its line forms and vocabulary, the Data Sensitivity field, and whose decision each thing is. Facts and reference only; the interview is the feature-prd-interview skill's.
